Forbad
fôr-băd´
v. (past tense of forbid: prohibited, hindered; rendering Greek diakoluo and koluo, Hebrew tsavah)
Old English forbeodan, to command against. The Authorized Version keeps the older past tense; the Greek is to hinder.

Biblical Definition

At Jordan: “John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?” (Mat 3:14). The disciples: “we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us” (Mar 9:38; Luk 9:49) — and the Lord said, Forbid him not. Balaam: “the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet” (2Pe 2:16). Israel came not near Ammon, “nor unto any place of the river Jabbok… nor unto whatsoever the LORD our God forbad us” (Deu 2:37).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) gives forbad as the past tense of forbid: to prohibit, to command to forbear; to oppose, to hinder.

expand to see more

FORBID, v.t. pret. forbad. To prohibit; to command to forbear or not to do.

2. To oppose; to hinder; to obstruct.

Key Scripture

Mat 3:14 — "But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?"

Mar 9:38 — "And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us."

Luk 9:49 — "And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us."

2Pe 2:16 — "But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet."

Deu 2:37 — "Only unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not, nor unto any place of the river Jabbok, nor unto the cities in the mountains, nor unto whatsoever the LORD our God forbad us."

Modern Corruption

Humility forbids what God appoints and party spirit forbids what God is doing, and the Lord overruled both with the same word.

expand to see more

John's forbidding was the humblest act in the Gospels and it was wrong. He had need to be baptized of Christ, and he said so, and the Lord's answer — suffer it to be so now — is the correction of every humility that stands in the way of an appointment of God. There is a false modesty that will not do what is commanded because it feels unworthy, and it is disobedience in a lowered voice. The disciples' forbidding in Mark 9 was the opposite fault: a man cast out devils in Christ's name and they forbad him because he followeth not us. Not Thee — us. The Lord's reply, Forbid him not, is the standing rebuke of the party that mistakes its own membership for the kingdom. The ass that forbad the madness of the prophet is the third and the funniest: when the man of God will not hear God, God will use a donkey.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek diakoluo (G1254), to hinder earnestly; koluo (G2967), to hinder, forbid; Hebrew tsavah (H6680), to command.

expand to see more

Greek diakoluo (G1254) — to forbid earnestly; Matthew 3:14 only.

Greek koluo (G2967) — to hinder, forbid; Mark 9:38–39, Luke 9:49–50, 2 Peter 2:16, Acts 10:47.

Hebrew tsavah (H6680) — to command; Deuteronomy 2:37, “whatsoever the LORD our God forbad us.”

Usage

"“John forbad him” — humility standing in the way of an appointment of God."

"“We forbad him, because he followeth not us” — not Thee: us."

"“The dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet” — when the man of God will not hear."
